"Renault, Susan" <susan.renault@velzengroup.edu> on 24/12/2024 10:59:38
To: "aime.ruiz@lumieresante.fr" <aime.ruiz@lumieresante.fr>
cc: "margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr" <margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr>
Subject: RE: Saint-Cyr Gros


Dear Aimé / Margaret,

Thanks for coming to Saint-Cyr to present an overview of the initiatives. We
enjoyed meeting you and your colleagues and look forward to working with
Lumière Santé. I would also like to pass on my team’s appreciation for the
dinner as well.

We wanted to give you an update on our clinical program and get some feedback
and additional information prior to our upcoming visit to Saint-Cyr on 17
January. Our program is going to be geared to the 3rd option you mentioned. We
plan on addressing some part of Care Solutions business. We are considering
two options regarding this topic and would like to pursue either (i) how
patients are admitted and recommending new procedures and ways to enhance
outpatient services, OR (ii) studying the supply chain for medical supplies
and coming up with recommendations for areas for further investment.

However, we would like to get some more information on the Outpatient Services
before truly scoping the program. We are also very open to suggestions,
especially if you had a much broader or different scope in mind; so please let
us know.

We have not yet reviewed the introductory information received last week, but
here are the questions we have specific to the Care Solutions unit:

Can we look at its overall business plan or a more detailed summary than is in
the annual report? What is the pricing philosophy/overall structure? Who are
the patients and how are they admitted? What would the patients be doing if
they did not come to Lumière Santé? What are the international expansion plans
and capabilities? Is there any important regulatory summary information we can
have?

If this information is not already covered in the review material you sent,
will you be able to recommend other sources where we may find such
information?

After we have reviewed the material sent to us recently, we may want to
schedule a phone call with you and/or one of your colleagues directly involved
in Care Solutions business. I would like to call you in the new year to
discuss this further. In the meantime, please feel free to call me at +33 4 59
27 70 77 if you need any information.

Regards,
Outpatient Services Task Force
Ram
Dennis
Jason
Omar
Steve
Clay

Subject: Ironclad vs. Titan Hauler, per Summit Logistics
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Summit Logistics' Ironclad debuted several years ago as a premium iteration of
the best-selling Titan Hauler bulk carrier. The issue was, the Titan Hauler
could be just as capable as the Ironclad and, in some specs, was even more
costly. For 2024, Summit Logistics has sought to further differentiate their
bulk transport from the popular Titan Hauler. The outcome is a solid carrier,
with enhanced handling capabilities and generous feature offerings.

This near-premium bulk hauler comes with either a 5,000 kW diesel engine
producing 2,500 kW or a 6,200 kW variant delivering 3,000 kW. Both engines are
paired with a six-speed automated gearbox. The new 6,200 kW option offers
substantial and smooth power delivery, but fuel efficiency is modest. The
Ironclad has been redesigned inside and out, and the results are impressive.
Now clearly distinct from the Titan Hauler from the bow forward, its
"EdgeLine" design theme includes a matte-finished grille and bold LED
navigation lights. Meanwhile, the interior gains brushed steel accents,
lending a distinctive, high-tech feel to this former Titan Hauler lookalike.

Improvements to the Ironclad extend beyond aesthetics. An all-new independent
rear suspension featuring a patented port-frame architecture debuts this year.
This design allows the cargo deck to lower by 180mm—making room for an
additional container tier—while increasing ground clearance to 235mm.
Simultaneously, ride comfort and handling have been significantly enhanced.
The Ironclad now feels more stable during transit and exhibits flatter turning
characteristics. A 65mm wider chassis improves handling further, while
increasing operator cabin space. Noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) have
also been reduced in the 2024 Ironclad. A 50% decrease in air infiltration
into the cabin and a refined automated transmission create a quieter operating
environment, although some vibration from the available all-wheel-drive system
is still noticeable through the floor.

New convenience features in the Ironclad include a standard six-way
power-adjustable operator seat, along with optional adjustable control pedals,
heated driver seats, and heated side mirrors. Among the Ironclad’s new safety
features are optional side curtain airbags, a reinforced hull structure, and a
lower front bumper for improved collision compatibility with other bulk
carriers. Later in the year, rollover protection sensors and a new GripTrac
traction and stability control system will also become available.

The Ironclad’s strengths lie in its feature-rich specification, powerful
engine options, and upgraded rear suspension. There are many bulk carriers on
the market, but if you want a Titan Hauler yet can’t stomach the idea of
owning the old reliable of bulk logistics, the Ironclad just might be the
right fit.

Well, I can't believe another year has passed, but it has. Sunday, October 27th is the Juvenile Diabetes Walk for a Cure! Again this year, I'm recruiting walkers for my team or simply asking for your support. I know you hate to hear those pleading calls for more of your money, but I'm going to ask anyway - most of you know me well! You see I have to. As an insulin dependent diabetic myself, it is my obligation to do what I can to support every effort to find a cure for this disease which affects so many adults and children! I know many of you see me deal with this disease everyday as I face it each time I put food in my mouth. I follow my meals religiously with a shot of insulin along with several finger sticks a day to check my blood sugar. It was only 4 years ago that I was diagnosed with diabetes, but your dollars are making a difference. Within 2 years, they are expecting to be able to release insulin that can be inhaled which would eliminate the painful injections.

I know that you have been inundated with organizations seeking your support to fund their projects and this has been especially true this year, but I hope that you will consider BrasiLog one of the few that you continue to support as I do. Please consider joining my team or one of the many BrasiLog teams and help us find a cure for Diabetes! A BrasiLog t-shirt will be given to each walker or sponsor who contributes R$25,00 or more! If R$25,00 isn't in your budget, you can purchase a "Support Ribbon" for only R$5,00 and it will be posted at the BrasiLog headquarters on October 25th. As always, your contributions are matched by BrasiLog! Thanks for your support and I hope to see you on the 28th!

Letícia Alves

	Thomas Gade 23/05/2024 09:26 AM 	   To: Chakradhar Lala
cc: Nihal Karan, Ekantika Nagarajan, Reyansh Krish, Hardik D Pal
Subject: RE: Greenfield Agricultural Initiative


Chakradhar, Nihal, Reyansh and I were on site with Viraj Vyas last week.
Nihal mentioned Viraj might think all suppliers, including direct farmers,
should bear the increase you noted. Nihal? This is good from a compliance
risk perspective since if all suppliers are treated equally, our direct
farmers who shifted to cooperative supply cannot claim unfair treatment.
Conversely, if they must pay because they reverted to cooperative sourcing,
they may seek reimbursement from us. If the increase is to recover costs from
the government procurement between 01/02/24-30/03/25, and direct farmers are
exempt, FarmPartnerships could face significant exposure to its partners. We
may need to revise our approach accordingly.
-----Original Message-----
From:  Lala, Chakradhar
Sent: Thursday, 23 May 2024 08:48 AM
To: Karan, Nihal; Bala, Peter; Sura, Qabil; Gade, Thomas; Greenfield Farms,
Pune; Harvest Zone, Nashik; Stoness, AgriIndia Commodities Desk; Bakhshi,
Tamara
Cc: Brahmbhatt, Vedhika; Pal, Hardik; Hora, Ronith; Mangat, Vrinda; Krish,
Reyansh
Subject: Greenfield Agricultural Initiative


AgriIndia’s recent filing confirms that the MSP freeze of ₹6.5 per kg does
not apply to direct farmers.

In hearings on AgriIndia's potential price revision for large suppliers:
AgriIndia has proposed to allocate all retained stock to small suppliers
(below 100 quintals). Large suppliers would be served by government
procurement or be direct farmers. Several stakeholders have significant
concerns with this. AgriIndia calculated the expected price increase under
their plan as ₹2.86 per kg. If large suppliers receive a share of retained
stock, the increase rises to ₹2.99 per kg. In that case, large suppliers
retain an MSP adjustment (related to long-term contracts and stranded costs)
which they would lose otherwise. Our role is to seek an order 1) excluding
direct farmers from any increase (the proposed ₹2.86) 2) excluding them from
any surcharge related to undercollection from the freeze (amount still
unknown) 3) prorating the surcharge if applicable.

-----Original Message-----
From: Bailey, Ann
Sent: Thursday, 7 November 2024 19:25
To: Cole, Elliot; Russell, Kirsty
Subject: Company Secretary Replacement

As you probably know, I will officially retire on 31 December 2024; so the
meeting on 11 November will be my last and a good time to appoint my
successor. Thanks for letting me continue as your company secretary after
stepping down from that role at Halcyon Mutual Bank. I don't think I could
have stopped "cold turkey," and I loved Halcyon because of my fondness for
the board members and most of the senior management. (I’ll reserve comments
on some who are no longer here.) I have really enjoyed the role since
Hugh-the-Man got involved, and the improved morale and financial results
show how positive that was for the bank. I have also long admired Sterling
Trust and enjoyed working with Oliver Leonard. So, it is my hope and sincere
recommendation that Oliver be selected to succeed me. He has repeatedly
shown he is capable of the role—in fact, he’s been doing most of the work
for a long time, except taking the minutes, which he has taken over more
than once. He’s a person of integrity, loyalty, and dedication, and I know
the Board likes him. I hope you both agree. I’ll miss you all, and Valerie,
I’d love to have lunch with you and Oliver anytime. I’m also available for
any help or advice I can offer. Thanks again. Much love, Kathryn Archer

Subject: Catherine Storey for Corporate Compliance Transactions
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I spoke with each of you a couple of weeks ago, and this issue was deferred
due to other urgent matters. However, everyone agreed that a fixed cutoff
Gilbert would be suitable for compliance transaction approvals.

The best approach would be to set a daily cutoff at 4pm (to get a sense of
volume, I reviewed yesterday’s activity to see how many approvals were
submitted after 4pm London Gilbert. There were three Corporate unit cases and
two Compliance unit cases submitted). After 4pm, any pending approvals would
automatically roll over to the following business day. That said, for those
approvals not deferred after 4pm, the various advisory teams must remember
these count as the next day’s work. I’m unsure how the procedures in the
Litigation practice would need to be adjusted for the daily status reports,
since the official records wouldn’t reflect these late approvals. Could the
Litigation team run supplementary reports to ensure the advisory desks have
accurate case statuses each morning?

I would welcome any feedback you have, and please confirm whether a 4pm
cutoff works for your respective teams.

Danielle
x36557

Eric – are there any concerns around the Compliance Procedure Review?
Mary – we touched on this briefly a few weeks ago... any updates?

BP 1188
Saint-Fons, Lyon 69568-1188

Hôpital Lumière

10 mars 2025

I am writing to formalize your invitation to attend, participate, and speak
at the SIAM Regional Healthcare Innovation Workshop. A time slot of thirty
minutes is allocated for invited presentations with an additional ten
minutes for discussion. The workshop, funded under the auspices of the Santé
et Recherche grant to SIAM, will not be a standard healthcare conference
with representatives from hospitals, academia, and public health agencies
presenting their latest studies. Instead, the meeting will emphasize the
clinical innovations and technologies currently applied in private
healthcare and research institutions. Additionally, the event will focus on
the mechanisms facilitating collaboration and knowledge exchange between
hospitals, universities, and public health organizations.

The workshop will be held at the Institut Médico-Légal de Lyon, from 25 to
28 April. The Fondation Lumière will provide support for travel expenses as
well as accommodation and meals for invited speakers. We would be happy to
assist with travel arrangements if needed.

We hope you can accept our invitation. If so, please send us a presentation
title, a brief abstract, and a list of any technical equipment required.

We look forward to welcoming you at the Centre de Conférences Lumière.

Sincerely

Christophe Rivière
Specialist
Lumière Santé SAS
+33 4 72 00 11 22
25 rue de la Santé
69007 Lyon

Dixon, Harry M Collins, Sandra Wood
cc:
Subject: Electronic Transactions Agreement - revised

Attached is a revised version of the ETA omitting the distinction between
transactions on TelcoNet and transactions on NexTel. If Maple & Crown is
the only party permitted to post network services on TelcoNet, there is no
need for the special rules that we drafted for what was previously a
"many-to-many" matching platform. However, we will need to develop a
different set of GTCs for transactions that Maple & Crown closes on
TelcoNet, since the services transacted on TelcoNet are not likely to be
the type that conform to Maple & Crown’s standard GTCs.

Subject: Re: Tatjana Indication
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Klaus-Günter,
If you look at it from a NorthSea Wind Index perspective, how would this appear? I think he wants to price-floating with an index reference but needs some guidance on which NorthSea Wind Index basis to apply. It’s not a firm contract since he likely won’t finalize a deal, so it’s really more a market signal. A bit unusual, but the closer we price to the NorthSea Wind Index, the better our chances to secure the contract. We should present a strong indicative offer, subject to credit approval, etc. When it comes to locking in the contract, and he probably won’t given the lack of operational history for these turbines, who knows what the market price will be then.

Arno

Darren:
Congratulations on this well deserved appointment. Your leadership has
been a major factor in making Tasman Ridge the leading mining and
logistics company that it is and I am looking forward to seeing Tasman
Ridge move to even greater heights under that leadership in the future.
Congratulations again, Robert Smith

---------------------- Forwarded by John Hunt on
12/11/2024 10:10 AM ---------------------------

Robert Stanley
12/11/2024 06:02 AM

Sent by: Tasman Ridge Schneider
To: All Tasman Ridge Worldwide
cc:

Subject: Succession Plan

It is my great pleasure to announce that the Western Minerals Board has
accepted my recommendation to appoint Darren Richmond as chief executive
officer, effective at the time of their next board meeting on 10 February
2025. Darren will also retain his duties as president and chief operating
officer. I will continue as chairman of the Western Minerals Board and will
remain at Tasman Ridge, working with Darren on the strategic direction of
the company and our day-to-day global operations.

Darren will assume the role at a time when the company is hitting on all
cylinders and is positioned for phenomenal growth. He is clearly ready for
the job, and after 15 years as CEO of this great company, I’m ready for a
somewhat different role.

Our succession plan has been clear for some time. This has afforded Darren
and me the freedom to combine our strengths toward building a company that
continues to exceed everyone’s expectations, including our own. We look
forward to furthering that relationship as Darren expands his role.

There are no plans for any other changes in our management team nor broad
shifts in strategy and direction.

Please join me in congratulating Darren. I look forward to a great 2025.

Subject:	Results of the Insolvency Hearing for TCO's Issues With Corporate Lending

Here is a quick update on how the TCO insolvency hearing went last week regarding the Corporate Lending issues:

TCO agreed to withdraw the part of their motion related to Corporate Lending. The bank confirmed that Corporate Lending has been using their credit lines and settling payments since the insolvency petition date.
The £1.8 million claim that TCO had included in Halcyon's "set off amount" (i.e. the outstanding fees for Corporate Lending agreements until contract expiry) was removed from TCO's motion.
The minimum deposit balance monthly requirement should no longer be enforced by the bank (Note: Initially TCO seemed to be using Corporate Lending’s minimum balance to offset Credit Risk and Corporate Lending liabilities).

I recommend challenging TCO's operations team if they insist Corporate Lending must maintain a minimum balance. If you encounter issues, please inform me and I will engage our external legal team again.

Thanks,
Julia Owen

Subject: Kestrel/Strato Flag Football Invitation

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd. and Strato Berry are proud to sponsor the
2nd Annual Strato-Kestrel Flag Football Challenge on Saturday, November 16.
The purpose of this event is to raise money for both companies, and to enjoy
the competitive spirit of one of the longest rivalries in aerospace
manufacturing. This year's game marks the 107th meeting between Kestrel and
Strato, and, with a little luck, the AeroTech South Title will be on the
line!

Kestrel and Strato Berry are sponsoring the event, but we need your help as
participants and fundraisers. Contributions raised will benefit the general
employee scholarship fund for each company.

The details:
Date:    Saturday, November 16th

Time:    10:00 a.m. - approximately 4 p.m. (Warm up is at 9:30 am)

Location:   Falcon Fields (just off Avon Road, south of M32)

Food and Drinks:  Marshall’s BBQ (FREE - courtesy of Kestrel Aerospace
Components Ltd.)

Eligibility:   Full-time employees and/or their spouses
    (Players must have graduated from AeroTech University or Strato College)

Team Jerseys:  Provided by Kestrel and Strato Berry

Format:   7 players with at least 1 female player on the field at all times

Team Size: Recommend 8-10 players per team (no more than 10 per team).
Contact the team captains to sign-up. (Sign-up now to ensure your place on a
team)

Prizes:    Winning team receives 16 tickets to the Kestrel/Strato aerospace
conference in Bristol on Friday, November 22. Winning team also owns the
“AeroCup” trophy until next year!

Fundraising Goal: The committee has set a goal of raising £16,000 for each
company. This will require a contribution of £2,000 per team, plus an equal
amount from corporate matching funds.

Last year's event featured a last-minute comeback as Vector Dynamics
defeated the Kestrel Falcons Team 1 for the championship and took home the
tickets and the trophy. This year, expect the Falcons (and Strato Berry) to
come in with revenge on their minds!

Thanks to the generous gift from the AeroTech Alumni, who redirected their
donations to the Kestrel Foundation, we were able to permanently endow
scholarships dedicated to the memory of the 12 engineers who died in last
year's Falcon Plant incident. We believe this event is a great tradition for
both companies, and we are pleased to be able to raise important funds for
both institutions.

so I can explore other options.

Thanks,


Jay

Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Everyone,

I finally touched base with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National
Association of Agriculture Commissioners ("NAAC") regarding their involvement
on the commodity trading side, specifically with regard to Section 18 crop
export authorizations.

According to Tripti, there is no coordinated group effort that exists (i.e., a
commodities committee or an individual Commissioner taking the lead on export
issues). Individual Commissioners get involved, but that is all. For example,
Maharashtra Commissioner Simon Sridhar recently opposed Deccan Agro's
application for export authority, but the Agricultural Export Board still
granted Deccan Agro's petition.

Tripti recommends that we engage the Commissioners as much as possible. For
example, if we believe that local market competition is non-existent and we
have evidence to that effect, we should certainly convey that information to
the individual Commissioner and have him/her weigh in on our behalf. Tripti
recognizes that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. is pro-competitive and that
typically the Commissioners would be in agreement with our positions – so it's
something for us to keep in mind as we move forward. There's no guarantee that
the Export Board will listen to the Commissioners, but it may be worth a try.

If anyone has any thoughts or comments, please let me know. Thanks.

Hiral

Subject: Fw: Results of Meeting on Warehouse Zone Allocation Changes
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Sara,

Below is the memo I sent out 19/09 summarizing the meeting on 17/09. See the second bullet point in my summary. I recall Manuella couldn’t join that day, but Marcelo was very engaged during the discussions.

I couldn’t locate my copy. Luckily, Matteo still had his.

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Mendes, Matteo
Sent:	Monday, 16 December 2024 10:20
To:	Ferreira, Heitor
Subject:	FW: Results of Meeting on Warehouse Zone Allocation Changes

FYI

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Ferreira, Heitor
Sent:	Thursday, 19 September 2024 14:25
To:	Moraes, Sara; Machado, Manuella; Mendonça, Dom; da Cunha, Heitor; Mendes, Matteo; Câmara, Ryan; Vieira, Luiz Miguel; Novaes, Antônio; Lopes, Arthur Miguel; Oliveira, Pedro; Camargo, Levi; Cassiano, Marcelo; Souza, João Miguel; Cunha, Cecília; Porto, Sophie; Santos, Levi
Cc:	Cunha, Heitor; Campos, Daniel; Correia, Nina
Subject:	Results of Meeting on Warehouse Zone Allocation Changes

The following summarizes the results of our meeting......If you want to discuss further, please call me.

São Paulo in 3 logistics hubs by point
The decision was made to split the Central Warehouse zone into two regions; Guarulhos and North São Paulo, rather than 3 regions or allocating by point. If further divisions are needed later, we can address them then. System updates to WMS are needed. I’ve spoken with Daniel Campos and Heitor Cunha—they confirmed the changes are straightforward and can be done in a couple of days.
Luiz Miguel Vieira and I will identify which deferred shipment points fall under these new zones and then share the data with Daniel and Heitor.

Question:  Should we implement this change immediately or wait for the start of the peak shipping season?

Shift from ‘net zero’ inventory approach / Set minimum activity level
We agreed to hold off on this issue for now. The planned activity that drives allocation doesn’t always match actual warehouse flow. Usually, the flexibility of the São Paulo Hub lets Operations adjust to maintain the required minimum inbound/outbound at Guarulhos and North São Paulo. More analysis needed. Levi Camargo, Pedro Oliveira and I will keep monitoring system operations to decide if more changes are necessary.

Send alert when scheduled volume exceeds warehouse capacity
IT will update the scheduling system to add a check comparing the final scheduled volume to the warehouse’s operational capacity. If the scheduled volume exceeds capacity, I’ll get an email alert. This is to track how often and how severe this issue is. I’ll coordinate with Matteo Mendes to finalize this.

Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.=20

Unclear how this is going to increase crop supply, reduce demand, and
increase= =20 farmer choice. Still doesn’t make sense to us to have the
state buy a=20 deteriorating irrigation network instead of rural school
meals.

We don’t have enough details. There are several aspects that are interesti=
ng=20 and could use further study. Governor Rajesh needs to make the details
publ= ic=20 as soon as possible so people can understand the full
implications. For=20 instance, what happens to the Farm Supply contracts?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure farmers can make=
=20 their own crop decisions going forward. We know that Government=20
doesn’t know how to get this right. The right answer is giving farmers= =20
more choices, not fewer.

= If=20 the payments aren’t made in full, highly likely that we’ll see
involuntary=20 insolvency.

Too bad that this deal wasn’t done earlier. It could have saved a lot of=20

Why do you need to include the irrigation network purchase in this deal? May

Date: Mon, 27 Oct 2025 06:50:23 -0400
From: Danielle Robinson <danielle.robinson@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
To: Brittany Gardner <brittany.gardner@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Melissa Miller <melissa.miller@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Reginald Gonzales <reginald.gonzales@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Cc: Gwendolyn Glass <gwendolyn.glass@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Subject: Fw: Lakefront Power Adjustment for TW
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I'm not aware of any TW agreements that are arranged like this, but it's been some time since I reviewed the tariff schedules. Do any of you remember cases where this might happen?

Thanks,
Danielle

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Glass, Gwendolyn
Sent:	Thursday, October 16, 2025 1:38 PM
To:	Robinson, Danielle
Subject:	Lakefront Power Adjustment for TW


I believe that, back in 1998, TW changed how they managed Lakefront Power to ensure that Reservation would not pay Lakefront Power if it was discounted. That would have increased TW's margin on certain agreements. But, the margin impact dropped by over 50% in 2001, when the Reservation Lakefront Power charge fell from $0.0066/day TO $0.0030. It will decrease again in 2002 when Reservation Lakefront Power becomes $0.0018.

Do you have any estimate of how many dollars TW will "lose" due to the drop in Lakefront Power?
For single-part discounted rates, I would expect minimal impact. For instance, if the market rate is $0.10, TW couldn't get more than $0.10 for capacity, whether the max Lakefront Power surcharge was $0.0066 or $0.0018.

However, are there any long-term contracts where you bill Lakefront Power as part of the rate but do not remit it due to discounting?
For example, the discounted reservation rate is $0.20 plus Lakefront Power. TW billed $0.2066 in 2000 but $0.2030 in 2001 and $0.2018 in 2002.
As long as the total rate is below the max, TW retains the Lakefront Power portion, but revenue on the contract declines yearly as the Lakefront Power component decreases. (I don’t know how many agreements like this TW might have. The Hydropower Unit has some.)

From: Cameron Russell <cameron.russell@kestrelaero.co.uk>
To: Craig Stone <craig.stone@kestrelaero.co.uk>, Alex Clarke <alex.clarke@kestrelaero.co.uk>, Elliott Fowler <elliott.fowler@kestrelaero.co.uk>, Mark Charlton <mark.charlton@kestrelaero.co.uk>
Subject: Accomplishments for the First Six Months of 2025
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

My accomplishments for the first six months of 2025 include the following:

1.    AeroParts Manufacturing Compliance Forms -- provided key legal expertise and intellectual capital to rewrite component manufacturing compliance forms to be largely consistent with the supplier quality assurance templates.

2.   AeroSystems Component Recall and Liability Strategy -- led the legal and supplier quality teams across all Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd entities in minimising company credit exposure and liability risks. This required an expedited assessment of Kestrel’s contractual positions and coordination across business units to determine the best possible approach to terminate and then value all AeroSystems contracts.

3.    Implemented New Document Retention Policy for Bristol Manufacturing Facility -- led the resolution of many critical document retention issues and rolled out a new policy across company divisions at Kestrel Aerospace.

4.    Thought Leader on Risk Management Framework -- continued to develop legal technology for better management and reporting of legal risks across Kestrel. The Falcon Risk Index and legal risk ratings are two examples. These policies have been newly applied in Bristol and the Manufacturing unit to better evaluate and manage legal risks in those operations.

5.     Developing New Business Lines -- integral part in developing new business lines in titanium alloys, composites, avionics, and machining services by preparing compliance forms and formulating new ways to manage legal risks.

6.     Contract Review Projects -- projects involving numerous complex issues including the Stratocraft Engine II, Gloucester Assembly, AeroForge, SkyBolt Components and AeroDynamics Ltd.

7.     Management -- continued to build a contract-focused legal team that understands the underlying aerospace manufacturing businesses.

8.     New Generation of Master Agreements -- leading efforts with the Aerospace Legal Consortium in developing the next generation of master agreements which would be a single master for all aerospace components, whether physical or financial. This would reduce legal workload by half.

Thanks Thomas.? We shall make the additions you noted below.? AgroHarvest
(Oliver Chatura) will be providing testimony on grain procurement unbundling
for the cooperatives. I agree with you that the mass-market farm suppliers
should also include complementary testimony.? Although we discussed this
earlier, I did not receive any firm commitments from the farm suppliers that
they would sponsor such testimony - it may be an oversight on my part.?
Nonetheless, testimony by those in the market should include a discussion of
the benefits from GreenFields, CropCo, FarmLink, AgroTrade and the others.?
Might I suggest that AgriIndia, as a large mass-supplier itself, coordinate
this effort with the other farm partners ?

In addition, I want all settlement parties to look beyond testimony to the
hearings, which are scheduled to begin in little more than a month.? We will
need to make some time available during late May for practice panels
(assuming we are granted panel hearings) and individual practice
cross-examination.? At the same time, we also need to start thinking about
direct cross-examination of the SCGC/TURN parties (again, assuming we decide
to engage in full cross-examination of their settlement).? There is merit to
cross-examination of the opposing settlement since it is not very well
thought out, results in substantial cost-shifts, and is not consistent with
the Agricultural Regulatory Authority's most promising options.? On the other
hand, there is merit to limiting our cross, especially of Pranit, who will
use the witness box to grandstand.? It's something to think about.
